population: EGFR-mutant (sensitising with T790M, or exon 20 insertion)
note: Osimertinib's T790M-mutant cell, xenograft and transgenic-mouse models predicted tumour pEGFR loss and response that patients showed, while the rat/dog/hERG safety package twice cleared QT prolongation that patients then had.
label: NSCLC (EGFR-mutant TKIs)

engagement.model: T790M/sensitising-mutant NSCLC cells, xenografts and transgenic mice
engagement.note: Osimertinib inhibited mutant EGFR signalling in H1975 and PC9 cells and xenografts, sparing wild-type lines; no patient tumour pEGFR yet.
engagement.short: Mutant EGFR signalling blocked in mice
engagement.quote: Preclinically, the drug potently inhibits signaling pathways and cellular growth in both EGFRm(+) and EGFRm(+)/T790M(+) mutant cell lines in vitro, with lower activity against wild-type EGFR lines

engagement.model: T790M/sensitising-mutant NSCLC cells, xenografts and transgenic mice
engagement.note: Paired AURA biopsies (80-160 mg, day 15) showed osimertinib modulating phospho-EGFR pathway markers in T790M tumours, as the xenograft pEGFR readout predicted.
engagement.short: Tumour EGFR signalling fell in patient biopsies
engagement.quote: Osimertinib modulated key EGFR signaling pathways and led to increased immune cell infiltration.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; abstract gives no pEGFR effect size, and only 24 of 61 patients had evaluable paired biopsies (responders' tumours were often too small to sample).
engagement.reason: Patient tumour pEGFR moved as mice showed
engagement.judgement: Scored on the paired AURA biopsies rather than on response rate, because the model's PD readout was tumour pEGFR. Readout tier taken as proximal (the target's own phosphorylation), not direct occupancy.
engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour phospho-EGFR after dosing, xenograft vs patient biopsy

dose.model: Rat and dog toxicology with mouse xenograft efficacy
dose.note: No model-stated human efficacious exposure found; the dog's highest tolerated exposure was half the 80 mg exposure, yet patients had no DLT to 240 mg.
dose.quote: Plasma AUCs achieved in the dog study at the highest-tolerated dose of 6 mg/kg/day were approximately 0.48X those observed in patients who received the 80 mg daily oral dose.
dose.confidence_note: Cross 2014 read at abstract level; FDA pharmacology and clinical pharmacology reviews grepped for a mouse-to-human dose translation and none found.
dose.judgement: Left untested: activity from the lowest dose (20 mg) and a flat exposure-response (FDA ClinPharm review) mean any xenograft target was exceeded, but no source states one, so there is nothing to score. The tox species tolerated less than the human exposure (no margin stated), so decision 16 does not apply. Yates 2016 (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-16-0142) models mouse PK/PD only, after AURA.

dose.note: Monkey microdose PET showed osimertinib reaching brain far better than rociletinib or gefitinib; no human brain exposure measured yet.
dose.quote: Under positron emission tomography micro-dosing conditions, [11C]osimertinib showed markedly greater exposure in the cynomolgus monkey brain than [11C]rociletinib and [11C]gefitinib.
dose.judgement: Opens the brain-exposure track at the model's publication; brain exposure, not systemic PK, is this system's dose target.
dose.model: EGFR-mutant PC9 mouse brain-metastasis model with cynomolgus [11C]osimertinib microdose PET

dose.magnitude_basis: brain/blood exposure of [11C]osimertinib, monkey vs human PET
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the human paper does not itself set out the monkey comparison in its abstract, so this is a pairing. ODIN-BM (Ekman 2023, doi 10.1111/cts.13500) states it: 'These findings corroborate preclinical data and observations in healthy volunteers'; 1.5% ID in humans vs 1.3% ID in NHPs.
dose.note: Human [11C]osimertinib PET showed the drug crossing the intact blood-brain barrier, as the monkey PET predicted; ODIN-BM (2023) repeated it in patients with brain metastases.
dose.quote: This study in healthy volunteers shows that 11C-osimertinib penetrates the intact blood-brain barrier.
dose.judgement: Brain exposure placed in dose (was the model's exposure reached). Dated to the healthy-volunteer PET (epub April 2019), the first public human comparison; ODIN-BM 2023 changes no status.
dose.model: EGFR-mutant PC9 mouse brain-metastasis model with cynomolgus [11C]osimertinib microdose PET

efficacy.model: T790M/sensitising-mutant NSCLC cells, xenografts and transgenic mice
efficacy.note: Osimertinib caused profound, sustained regression of EGFR-mutant and EGFR-mutant/T790M xenografts and transgenic tumours.
efficacy.quote: translating into profound and sustained tumor regression in EGFR-mutant tumor xenograft and transgenic models.

efficacy.model: T790M/sensitising-mutant NSCLC cells, xenografts and transgenic mice
efficacy.note: AURA's primary endpoint, response in the expansion cohorts, was 61% in T790M-positive versus 21% in T790M-negative tumours; AURA3 then beat chemotherapy (PFS HR 0.30).
efficacy.quote: Among 127 patients with centrally confirmed EGFR T790M who could be evaluated for response, the response rate was 61% (95% CI, 52 to 70).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Janne 2015; primary endpoint (ORR, dose-expansion population) from the NCT01802632 registry record.
efficacy.judgement: Paired (model Cross 2014, patients AURA): the trial paper cites the preclinical work but does not compare. Regression in mice vs 61% ORR is a directional match. Kept 'same' through mobocertinib's EXCLAIM-2 failure because its exon 20 Ba/F3/PDX models are a different system and the status follows the best model; a stricter class-wide reading would turn the cell contra in 2025. Rociletinib's overstated response (FDA rejection 2016) was not scored: no trial failed its primary endpoint against a model prediction.

patient_trials.quote: The median duration of progression-free survival was significantly longer with osimertinib than with platinum therapy plus pemetrexed (10.1 months vs. 4.4 months; hazard ratio; 0.30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.23 to 0.41; P<0.001).

The EXCLAIM-2 trial did not meet its primary end point. The efficacy of mobocertinib was not superior to platinum-based chemotherapy for first-line treatment of patients with EGFR ex20ins+ advanced/metastatic NSCLC.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs objective response rate in patients

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The paper's AURA case reports are anecdotal, not a primary endpoint, so the cell opens untested.
efficacy.note: Osimertinib at clinically relevant doses caused sustained regression of PC9 brain metastases in mice; rociletinib did not.
efficacy.quote: Osimertinib demonstrated greater penetration of the mouse blood-brain barrier than gefitinib, rociletinib (CO-1686), or afatinib, and at clinically relevant doses induced sustained tumor regression in an EGFRm PC9 mouse brain metastases model
efficacy.judgement: Case reports in the same paper are not scored: no trial endpoint.
efficacy.model: EGFR-mutant PC9 mouse brain-metastasis model with cynomolgus [11C]osimertinib microdose PET

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse brain-metastasis regression vs leptomeningeal ORR by BICR
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. NCT02228369 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05). BLOOM is single-arm and dosed 160 mg, twice the label dose; the mouse model modelled parenchymal, not leptomeningeal, disease.
efficacy.population: EGFR-mutant NSCLC with leptomeningeal metastases after prior EGFR-TKI (T790M not required)
efficacy.note: BLOOM's primary objective, leptomeningeal ORR by blinded central review, was 62% on osimertinib 160 mg, matching the brain-metastasis model's predicted CNS activity.
efficacy.quote: Osimertinib showed meaningful therapeutic efficacy in the CNS and a manageable safety profile at 160 mg once daily in patients with EGFRm NSCLC and LM.

patient_trials.quote: LM ORR and DoR by neuroradiologic BICR were 62% (95% CI, 45% to 78%) and 15.2 months (95% CI, 7.5 to 17.5 months), respectively.

efficacy.judgement: Population: BLOOM's LM cohort is EGFR-sensitising-mutant after TKI, mostly not T790M-selected, so it sits at the edge of the draft's T790M/exon 20 population; kept because the tile's class is all EGFR inhibitors and the draft's narrowing is an open rule question. Paired, not stated: BLOOM does not cite the mouse result as a prediction.
efficacy.model: EGFR-mutant PC9 mouse brain-metastasis model with cynomolgus [11C]osimertinib microdose PET

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. 2016 is a proxy from the Phase 1/2 start (NCT02716116, 2016-06-16); the model was published in 2021.
efficacy.note: Mobocertinib's exon 20 insertion cell and PDX models predicted tumour regression; Phase 1/2 (NCT02716116) opened June 2016.
efficacy.quote: Mobocertinib inhibited viability of various EGFRex20ins-driven cell lines more potently than approved EGFR TKIs and demonstrated in vivo antitumor efficacy in patient-derived xenografts and murine orthotopic models.
efficacy.judgement: Opening year is the first-in-human start, since the model must have preceded it.
efficacy.model: EGFR exon 20 insertion Ba/F3 lines, patient-derived xenografts and orthotopic mice (mobocertinib)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regression vs confirmed ORR by IRC
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. NCT02716116 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05). PubMed lists epub 2021-12-16; FDA accelerated approval (Sept 2021) was the same year.
efficacy.note: The PPP cohort's primary endpoint, confirmed ORR by independent review, was 28% at 160 mg, enough for accelerated approval: activity as the models predicted.
efficacy.quote: In this open-label, phase 1/2 nonrandomized clinical trial, mobocertinib was associated with clinically meaningful benefit in patients with previously treated EGFRex20ins-positive mNSCLC, with a manageable safety profile.

patient_trials.quote: with confirmed ORR of 28% (95% CI, 20%-37%) by IRC assessment and 35% (95% CI, 26%-45%) by investigator assessment

efficacy.judgement: A single-arm ORR of 28% against xenograft regression is direction-only agreement; scored same because the primary endpoint was met.
efficacy.model: EGFR exon 20 insertion Ba/F3 lines, patient-derived xenografts and orthotopic mice (mobocertinib)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS hazard ratio vs platinum chemotherapy
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. NCT04129502 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05). The failure was first announced by Takeda press release in October 2023 (tier 5); that release was not verified here, so the entry is dated to the JCO paper.
efficacy.note: EXCLAIM-2 crossed futility: PFS 9.6 months in each arm (HR 1.04) against platinum chemotherapy; Takeda withdrew mobocertinib.
efficacy.quote: The EXCLAIM-2 trial did not meet its primary end point. The efficacy of mobocertinib was not superior to platinum-based chemotherapy for first-line treatment of patients with EGFR ex20ins+ advanced/metastatic NSCLC.
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra per the dose/efficacy table (reached, failed, abandoned). The models never tested an active comparator, which the checker raised as an open rule question; if the ruling is 'untested', this entry changes. Year may move to 2023 once the press release is verified.
efficacy.model: EGFR exon 20 insertion Ba/F3 lines, patient-derived xenografts and orthotopic mice (mobocertinib)

efficacy.note: Ba/F3 and PDX data placed PACC mutations as resistant to third-generation TKIs such as osimertinib and sensitive to second-generation TKIs.
efficacy.quote: In vivo, we also observed that NSCLC patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) containing G719A mutations were resistant to the third-generation TKI osimertinib, but most sensitive to the second-generation TKI poziotinib
efficacy.judgement: Model and patient comparison appear in the same paper; opening entry marks the model.
efficacy.model: Ba/F3 panel of 76 EGFR mutants grouped by structure (classical-like, T790M-like, Ex20ins-L, PACC), with PDX

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Ba/F3 IC50 class vs time to treatment failure by TKI generation
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8481125). Third-generation arm is small and pooled; whether every patient there received osimertinib (a member) rather than another third-generation drug is not stated in the text read. TTF, not a trial endpoint.
efficacy.population: NSCLC with PACC EGFR mutations, retrospective MD Anderson and Moffitt cohorts
efficacy.note: Patients with PACC mutations had shorter time to treatment failure on third-generation TKIs (4.1 months) than second-generation (21.7 months), as the Ba/F3 grouping predicted.
efficacy.quote: patients with PACC mutations treated with second-generation TKIs had a significantly longer TTF than patients treated with either first- or third-generation TKIs (21.7 months versus 10.0 months and 4.1 months, respectively
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the TTF data are from treated patients whose outcomes predated the Ba/F3 grouping, and the paper says the groups 'retrospectively predict' outcomes. PACC lies outside the draft's T790M/exon 20 population; kept because the class is all EGFR inhibitors and population is an open rule question. model_kind 'animal' for murine Ba/F3 cells plus PDX; no in-vitro enum exists.
efficacy.model: Ba/F3 panel of 76 EGFR mutants grouped by structure (classical-like, T790M-like, Ex20ins-L, PACC), with PDX

efficacy.population: Advanced lung cancer, osimertinib cohort after prior EGFR-TKI
efficacy.note: Organoids grown from each patient's effusion were tested against the osimertinib that patient then received.
efficacy.quote: In the osimertinib cohort, osimertinib was selected as the next-line treatment for 12 patients ( Figure 3 C), and the sensitivity of osimertinib was tested on 15 LCOs generated from these patients ( Figure 3 D).
efficacy.judgement: First use dated to the publication; the study's own enrolment dates were not checked.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions, drug sensitivity test

efficacy.magnitude_basis: organoid osimertinib IC50 vs best response (PR vs PD), ROC AUC 0.94
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9975107). Twelve patients, single centre; treatment was chosen by guidelines, not by the organoid, and whether organoid results were read before response assessment is not stated, so retrodiction is left false with low confidence. Not a trial endpoint.
efficacy.population: Advanced EGFR-mutant lung cancer receiving next-line osimertinib (incl. T790M-positive)
efficacy.note: Organoid osimertinib IC50 separated responders from progressors (ROC AUC 0.94, n=12 patients), including a T790M patient the organoid called resistant who progressed.
efficacy.short: Organoid IC50 separates PR from PD
efficacy.quote: Generally, the IC 50 of the progression disease (PD) and partial response (PR) groups could be distinguished significantly, with an area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.94 in ROC analysis
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level: the organoid did not choose treatment, but its call was compared with each patient's response. Not marked retro because organoids were derived at progression before the next-line osimertinib was given.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions, drug sensitivity test

safety.model: hERG assay with rat and dog toxicology and dog cardiovascular telemetry
safety.note: The pre-IND safety package (hERG, dog telemetry, 13-week rat and dog studies) ran before AURA opened in 2013.
safety.quote: The Sprague Dawley rat and the Beagle dog were the primary models used to investigate the safety of osimertinib.
safety.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: AURA (NCT01802632) began in 2013, so the package existed by then.

safety.model: hERG assay with rat and dog toxicology and dog cardiovascular telemetry
safety.note: hERG IC50 sat above free drug levels and dog telemetry was clean, yet patients had concentration-dependent QTc prolongation (2.7% >60 ms) that entered the label.
safety.quote: data from the in vivo cardiovascular safety pharmacology study did not suggest clear effects on QTc prolongation at tolerable doses. QTc prolongation has occurred at a low frequency in clinical trials.
safety.confidence_note: Dog exposures at tolerated doses reached only about half the human AUC, so the telemetry could not test the clinical exposure; the hERG margin call was made at the clinical free Cmax.
safety.judgement: Scored contra on QT, not on ILD: rats and dogs showed only alveolar macrophage infiltrates, not pneumonitis, so their silence on the 3.3% ILD is not clearly a harm the species could show. Mobocertinib repeated the miss (FDA 2021 multidisciplinary review: hERG >5 uM and clean dog ECGs, then a boxed QTc/torsades warning; 'The reason for the discrepancy between the nonclinical and clinical QT data is unknown'), which keeps the cell contra. Cardiomyopathy (1.4%) was hinted at by equivocal reduced contractility in dogs and guinea pigs, so it is not counted as a miss.
safety.magnitude_basis: QTc effect: none predicted vs median +14 ms at 80 mg and label warning
